editorial:
Imagine you are hanging out by the beach when people start vanishing into thin air. When the bodies finally wash up, they are just clean bones, which is pretty creepy. You get to follow Dr. Turner, a scientist who thinks a big company building a tunnel under the bay messed up the water. He believes their pollution turned a normal octopus into a giant, hungry monster. The vibe is very much like those old monster movies where things go wrong because of greedy businessmen and bad science, making it a fun ride if you like retro scares.

You will notice the special effects are a bit cheesy by today's standards, but that is actually part of the charm. The pacing is steady, and while the acting is a bit stiff, the suspense keeps you guessing. It is perfect for a lazy Saturday night with friends. If you want the best experience, try adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection for the best colors. Otherwise, renting it on Apple TV is a great way to see if you like this kind of campy horror before buying it.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up with a big showdown between the humans and the giant octopus. After several people are eaten, the survivors manage to fight back. They use explosives and traps to finally kill the creature, stopping the killing spree for good. It turns out the company was definitely to blame for the mutation. Once the monster is dead, the town can finally breathe again, and the secret pollution is exposed to the world.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old school monster movies and bad special effects.
